chapter: Old bandleaders, drummers and Edgewater years
title: Police shows at the Roosevelt and double feature theaters
summary: Discussion of Pinky's police shows, the union rules around the Roosevelt band, and what a double feature meant for theater bands.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well the funny thing about the police shows was that these guys, and this is the most ridiculous thing of all, Wiley Harris who was one of the promoters of the show, every year they had to take a trip to the Edgewater Beach Hotel to hear the band to see if it would be acceptable to play for the police PMBA, Police Mutual Benefit Association. And he and a couple of other guys would have to go up to Chicago to hear the band to see if it was alright for them. Regardless of who it was, this band was coming to the Roosevelt Hotel and that was the band that they were going to get whether they liked it or not because that's the band that Seymour Weiss gave it to him. And he said, he said, Seymour Weiss set a, what do you call it, I can't remember, a statue before by leaving the band off to play Monday night for the PMBA, the Roosevelt Hotel Orchestra. I mean the band that was playing at the Roosevelt. They would give him permission to go up there and play that show, it was alright for the union to give him that. But if the band wanted to play another job, the band that was on a job like Kellner's band or any of the other bands that wanted to have a, that there was a night off that they could play another job, they wouldn't allow it. And I think there was an unjust situation with the whole thing.
I got a note here that says something about double headliner bill. Oh yeah, I found that on the newspaper. What was the double headliner bill, do you know, in a theater, like in Vaudeville?

Oh yeah, double headliner, you had two feature pictures. Oh I see. Yeah, you had two feature pictures. Oh, so that had nothing to do with the band. No, no, no, no, no. The band would be in between each one of them. Oh, in between the, oh yeah.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. And they mentioned the four Camerons.
I remember the name. Yeah. But I couldn't, I couldn't. Well it, it, I found the thing in the newspaper, it had quite a write up on the, on that.

Yeah, well the double feature was, that was two, two, two full, full pictures. Oh, double feature, it's like that. Yeah, two, two out pictures. Did I tell you? Incidentally, Charlie Duke was a good drummer. Yeah. I liked him. Charlie Pager, your good solid tempo. And anytime you played the good solid tempo, I liked it. You do too. That's right. I was one of his parmars. I was one of his parmars. What about Ferdinand Trombino? That's, that's another story. I never will forget Joe Loi Canna playing saxophone on there.
